annotations.text:
The calendar, redrawn — day and week.

Three things change. Blocks get a height, so an hour looks like an hour and a ten-minute habit does not. Your day and the agents' work get their own lanes, so the machine never pushes your afternoon around. And the sidebar carries what has no duration: the month, the layers, the goal deadlines, today's reminders.

The day view today draws every item as a chip inside a slot row, coloured by status. That is why it reads as a list with times rather than a day.

Static mockups, on this machine's own names and numbers. Dark by default; there is a light switch above each artboard.

The ◌ marker means nothing is behind it yet.

It is on the micro-habits strip, the habits counter and the agent-hours counter, and it is on three fields in the composer. The Gaps board says exactly what each one would cost.

Nothing else on these boards needs a new table — the redraw runs on the data calendar_range already returns.

Five kinds, five tab bodies — because the fields genuinely differ.

A focus session has no repeat. A habit has no start time. A handover has an owner.

One refusal, kept from schedule.rs: there is no "wake agent X at 9am". A naked agent on a timer has no goal, nowhere to write and nobody to ask. Asking a bot is the supported shape of that wish.

Week is the same day, thinner. Two lanes will not fit seven times, so agent time collapses into a gutter down each column — green for a run, red where one failed.

Everything after now is hollow and dashed. The future is intent, not history, and should never be drawn as though it happened.

Built 5 September, with one change from this board: the habit ticks are not there yet. Habits have no table (step 3), and a row of empty ticks is a promise, not a feature.

Read this board before agreeing to the picture.

Step 1 is a redraw — no schema change, no new command, today's data drawn honestly.

Two entries are real work: micro-habits need their own table, and agent working time is only true for today until sessions are written down. The "1 meeting" card should be cut: there are no people, no invitations and no attendance behind it.
